KitchenAid Gourmet Meat Tenderizer vs OXO Good Grips: Which Meat Tenderizer Deserves a Spot in Your Drawer?

The KitchenAid Gourmet Multi-Sided Meat Tenderizer ($9.79) and the OXO Good Grips Meat Tenderizer ($14.99) are two of the most practical kitchen tools you can own. One costs 35% less. Does the other justify the premium? We broke it down side by side.

Published August 2026 · Based on verified Amazon product data

A good meat tenderizer is one of those tools that quietly makes everything you cook better. Chicken breasts cook evenly. Steaks don't fight back. Pork chops stay juicy instead of dry. And cheap cuts of beef turn into something that feels like a splurge.

The two tools we're comparing here approach the job differently. The KitchenAid Gourmet Multi-Sided Meat Tenderizer is a textured mallet with a flat side for pounding and a textured side for tenderizing — classic, no-frills design. The OXO Good Grips Meat Tenderizer uses a bladed needle design that pierces the meat to break down connective tissue from the inside.

They're both good. But they work very differently. Here's when each one makes sense.

Quick Verdict

Buy the KitchenAid Gourmet Meat Tenderizer (our pick) if: You want a versatile tool that does double duty — pound chicken breasts flat for even cooking, tenderize steaks and pork chops, and even crush crackers or nuts with the flat side. At $9.79, it's the most value per tool in your kitchen drawer.

Buy the OXO Good Grips if: You primarily cook thicker cuts of beef and want deeper tenderization without flattening the meat. The bladed design is excellent for breaking down connective tissue in tougher cuts like chuck or flank steak, and the ergonomic handle is genuinely comfortable for extended use.

Our pick: The KitchenAid Gourmet Multi-Sided Tenderizer. For $9.79, you get a tool that does everything — pounding, tenderizing, and even crushing. The OXO is better at one specific thing (deep needle tenderization), but the KitchenAid is better at everything else most home cooks actually need.

Our Pick 🏆 KitchenAid Gourmet Multi-Sided Meat Tenderizer

The KitchenAid Gourmet Meat Tenderizer is a study in doing the simple things well. It's a traditional mallet-style tenderizer with a stainless steel head that has two distinct sides: a flat surface for pounding and a textured side with raised pyramids for tenderizing. The handle is sturdy, the head is weighty enough to do real work, and it's dishwasher safe.

What makes it punch above its price tag is versatility. The flat side isn't just for chicken — it's excellent for crushing garlic cloves, crackers for breading, or even softening butter. The textured side breaks down meat fibers efficiently without shredding the surface. And at just $9.79, it's one of the cheapest genuinely useful upgrades you can make to your kitchen.

The stainless steel head is rust-resistant and easy to clean — a real advantage over cast iron tenderizers that need immediate drying. The handle is comfortable for short sessions, though if you're tenderizing several pounds of meat at once, you might want a thicker grip.

It also comes from KitchenAid, a brand with decades of kitchen credibility. While this isn't their flagship product tier, the build quality is solid and consistent with what you'd expect from a brand that knows kitchens.

Key specs: Stainless steel head, dual-sided (flat + textured), 9-inch length, dishwasher safe, rust-resistant, ~0.5 lbs.

🔪 OXO Good Grips Bladed Meat Tenderizer

$14.99 on Amazon

The OXO Good Grips takes a completely different approach. Instead of pounding and surface tenderizing, it uses a bladed needle design — 48 thin stainless steel needles that pierce the meat to break down connective tissue and muscle fibers from the inside. The result is tender meat that keeps its shape and thickness.

This is a specialized tool for a specific job. If you frequently cook tougher cuts of beef — flank steak, skirt steak, chuck roast — the OXO's needle system does something the KitchenAid mallet can't: it tenderizes deep into the meat without flattening it. For chicken breasts or pork chops, it's less useful than the mallet, but for beef, it's arguably more effective.

The handle is where OXO's legendary ergonomics shine. The large, soft, non-slip grip is genuinely comfortable even during extended use. If you're tenderizing multiple steaks for a dinner party, your hand won't cramp. The needles are rust-resistant and the base is dishwasher safe, though the needles do require thorough cleaning to remove meat residue from between them.

Key specs: 48 stainless steel needles, piercing design (keeps meat shape), soft non-slip handle, dishwasher safe, ergonomic grip.

Where the KitchenAid Wins

Versatility is the name of the game. The KitchenAid isn't just a meat tenderizer — it's a multi-tool for your kitchen. The flat surface is perfect for pounding chicken breasts to uniform thickness (bye-bye, dry edges and raw centers). But it also crushes garlic cloves in one hit, breaks up graham crackers for pie crusts, and even works as a quick nut cracker in a pinch.

The price is hard to beat. At $9.79, the KitchenAid costs 35% less than the OXO. That's a savings of $5.20 — enough to buy a second one for a vacation home or to add a good kitchen scale to your cart. For most home cooks, the $9.79 price tag means this tool pays for itself the first time you cook evenly-thickened chicken breast instead of the usual uneven mess.

Zero learning curve. Pick it up, whack the meat. The flat side flattens, the textured side tenderizes. There's no technique to learn — you don't need to worry about pressing at the right angle or depth. This matters more than you think. Bladed tenderizers require consistent, even pressure across the whole surface. A mallet is foolproof.

Easier to clean thoroughly. The KitchenAid's smooth surfaces rinse clean in seconds. Meat fibers can't get stuck between needles because there are no needles. This is a small thing until you're scrubbing raw chicken residue out of 48 tiny gaps after dinner.

Where the OXO Wins

Deep tenderization without flattening. This is the OXO's superpower. When you're cooking a flank steak for fajitas or a chuck roast for Sunday dinner, you want the meat to stay thick and juicy — not get pounded into a thin sheet. The 48 needle system breaks down connective tissue deep inside the meat while keeping the surface intact. The result is tender beef that still feels like a steak.

The ergonomic handle is genuinely excellent. OXO's entire brand is built around comfortable, accessible kitchen tools, and the Good Grips tenderizer is a perfect example. The large, soft, non-slip handle fits naturally in your hand and reduces hand fatigue during extended use. If you're tenderizing multiple pounds of meat, you'll notice the difference within the first 30 seconds.

Better for thick cuts of beef. If your cooking revolves around beef — steaks, roasts, braising cuts — the OXO approach is simply more effective than a mallet. The needles penetrate deep enough to break down collagen in tougher cuts, which is exactly what you want for a slow-cooked pot roast or a properly tenderized flank steak. The mallet can't reach that deep without turning the meat into a pounded mess.

The $5.20 Question

The price difference here is $5.20. That's small enough that you could honestly justify buying both — the KitchenAid for everyday chicken and pork, the OXO for beef-centric meals. But if you're picking one, here's how to think about it:

If you cook chicken and pork 2-3 times a week: Get the KitchenAid. It's cheaper, more versatile, and does exactly what you need it to do. The flat side is excellent for evening out chicken breast thickness, which is the single most impactful thing you can do for better weeknight dinners.

If you cook beef steaks and roasts several times a month: Consider the OXO. The needle system genuinely makes a difference with tougher cuts, and the ergonomic handle is a real quality-of-life upgrade if you're tenderizing regularly.

If you're on a budget: Get the KitchenAid without hesitation. It handles 90% of what the average home cook needs from a tenderizer for 35% less money. The OXO is the specialist tool; the KitchenAid is the everyday hero.

Pro tip: Whichever you buy, use plastic wrap or a zipper bag between the mallet and the meat. It prevents splatter, keeps your tool cleaner, and doesn't affect the tenderizing at all. For the OXO, always pierce through the plastic to avoid meat residue getting stuck in the needles.

Our Advice

The Bottom Line

The KitchenAid Gourmet Multi-Sided Meat Tenderizer is the better buy for 9 out of 10 home cooks. At $9.79, it's cheaper, more versatile, easier to clean, and does everything most people need from a meat tenderizer. The fact that it doubles as a pounder for chicken and a crusher for crackers and nuts makes it one of the best value tools in any kitchen drawer.

The OXO Good Grips is the specialist's choice. If you primarily cook beef and want deep tenderization without flattening, it's the better tool for that specific job. The ergonomic handle is outstanding. But for $5.20 more and narrower use cases, it's harder to recommend as a first tenderizer.

Save the $5.20. Get the KitchenAid. Use it for everything. Your chicken breasts — and your wallet — will thank you.
